overview.text: The Northwestern Garter Snake is a small, harmless garter snake of the Pacific Northwest of North America. Its stripe can be almost any colour - white, yellow, orange, red, green, turquoise or even blue.

identification.text: Small, with a stripe down the middle of the back that may be white, yellow, orange, red, green, turquoise or blue; some have small dark spots.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-western British Columbia in Canada, and western Washington, western Oregon and north-western California in the USA.

habitat.text: Sunny meadow edges surrounded by forest; in British Columbia also near fresh and salt water. On hot days it hides under stumps and rocks.

diet.text: Slugs, salamanders and frogs; near water also small fish.

recognise.text: Small garter snake with a stripe that can be red, orange, yellow, blue or green.
